metadata.title: Crypto exit-scam / Ponzi archetype + the Binance enforcement case (two DIFFERENT things, kept distinct)
metadata.frame: The recurring structure the user asked about: a platform (exchange, 'lending' program, or token) takes customer deposits, promises impossible returns or frictionless withdrawals, freezes withdrawals, and the operators vanish or the entity shuts down - funds gone, no product delivered. This block catalogs the canonical instances as a shared ARCHETYPE node (Crypto_Exit_Scam) and, SEPARATELY, records the Binance/CZ enforcement resolution. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION (anti-conflation): Binance is an operating exchange that pleaded to anti-money-laundering / sanctions failures - it is NOT an exit scam and did not abscond with customer funds. Conflating an AML case with a fund-stealing exit scam would be inaccurate; the two are modeled as different edge sets.
metadata.grade: per-edge (fact | contested). Enforcement outcomes and founder actions are documented (DOJ, FBI, court records, national regulators). Some loss amounts are disputed (Africrypt) or ranged (OneCoin) - noted per edge.
metadata.method: DOJ Office of Public Affairs (Binance $4B resolution, 2023); court sentencings (CZ Apr 2024; SBF; Kumbhani); FBI Ten Most Wanted (Ignatova); Turkish court (Ozer); Ontario Securities Commission (QuadrigaCX); contemporaneous reporting.

edges.notes: Nov 2023: Binance pleaded guilty and paid >$4.3B (one of the largest US corporate resolutions) for Bank Secrecy Act failures, operating an unlicensed money-transmitting business, and IEEPA sanctions violations (processed transactions for users in Iran/Cuba/Syria/Russian-occupied Ukraine). Coordinated with FinCEN, OFAC, and CFTC. This is an AML/sanctions case - NOT an exit scam; customer funds were not stolen (fact).

Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty to failing to maintain an effective AML program (BSA), resigned as CEO, paid a $50M personal fine, and was sentenced (Apr 30 2024, Judge Richard Jones, Seattle) to 4 months prison - far below the 36 months DOJ sought; released Sept 2024. Retained an estimated ~90% of Binance. Pardoned by President Trump in Oct 2025 (fact).

Self-styled 'Cryptoqueen'; founded/led OneCoin, a Ponzi disguised as crypto (from 2014) with NO real blockchain; raised ~$4B+ (reports range up to ~$19B) from 3M+ members. Vanished Oct 2017 en route Bulgaria->Athens; on the FBI Ten Most Wanted list (fact).
Archetype: sell a token with no product, take deposits via MLM recruitment, founder disappears (fact).

Founder/CEO of Thodex (Turkey); the exchange abruptly froze ~$2B for 400,000+ users (Apr 2021); Ozer fled to Albania 3 days before Istanbul raids; later extradited and sentenced to 11,196 years in Turkey (fact).
Operating exchange -> sudden withdrawal freeze -> founder flees with deposits (fact).

Founder of QuadrigaCX (Canada's largest exchange); ~$190M in customer funds became inaccessible when Cotten reportedly died in 2018 holding the sole private keys. The Ontario Securities Commission concluded it operated as a Ponzi; the death itself remains a subject of public doubt (fact of loss/OSC finding; death contested).
Exchange collapse with sole-custody keys -> funds unrecoverable; OSC found Ponzi characteristics (fact/contested-cause).

South African platform (Cajee brothers) promised ~10%/mo; ~$3.6B in BTC disappeared Apr 2021, blamed on a 'hack' - but staff were locked out of the back-end a week prior. Loss amount is DISPUTED (contested).
BCC 'lending program' promised up to ~40%/month; ~$2.4B Ponzi; collapsed early 2018 after cease-and-desist orders; founder Satish Kumbhani charged (SEC/DOJ), facing decades (fact).

The flagship exchange collapse: customer funds diverted to Alameda; Sam Bankman-Fried convicted of fraud, sentenced to 25 years (2024). Distinct from Binance (fraud/misappropriation vs AML failure) (fact).
